Has a registered dataset been rebuilt since it was registered?

Source: R/source_changed.R
source_changed.Rd

Says whether a study dataset's source file has changed since its current version was registered with register_data() or update_manifest(). Jobs keep reading the registered version until update_manifest() registers the rebuild, so a report can use this to say, before it reads any data, that a newer build is waiting.

It reads no data, but it hashes the source file and compares the SHA-256 with the one recorded at registration, so the answer is about the bytes: a touch that changed nothing is not reported, and a same-size replacement that kept the old modification time (a copy or restore that preserves dates) is. The cost is one pass over the source file. read_built() and update_manifest() make the same comparison, so every read of a registered dataset hashes its source once.

Usage

source_changed(cfg = study_config(), dataset = "study")

Arguments

cfg

List. A study manifest from study_config().

dataset

Character(1). Logical dataset name. Defaults to "study". "built" is a second name for "study".

Value

TRUE when the source differs from the registered version. FALSE when it matches, when the dataset has no registered dated version, or when the source file is missing, since jobs then keep reading the registered version and there is nothing newer to register.

See also

review_built() to compare the rebuild with the registered version, update_manifest() to register it.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("arrow", quietly = TRUE)) {
  root <- file.path(tempdir(), "source-changed-example")
  suppressMessages(study_setup(root, "Example", 1L, renv = FALSE))
  path <- file.path(study_dir("datasets", root), "example.csv")
  write.csv(data.frame(DEAD = c(1, 0, 0), IV_DEAD = 1:3), path, row.names = FALSE)
  suppressMessages(register_data("example.csv", root = root))
  source_changed(study_config(root))
  write.csv(data.frame(DEAD = c(1, 0, 0, 1), IV_DEAD = 1:4), path, row.names = FALSE)
  source_changed(study_config(root))
  unlink(root, recursive = TRUE)
}
